title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Invoicing a Work Order and Applying Payments
content:
## Clauses retired from this basis

The two clauses below are no longer in force, and neither the falling due of a charge nor the late fee
on demand service arrears is worked out from them today:

> The invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date, counted in calendar days with the invoice day excluded and the due day included, and the account's own credit terms apply only where the program has no term of its own.

> An invoice unpaid past its due day carries the tier's late fee on the unpaid amount for each month or part month it stays unpaid.

## The invoice

Demand work is invoiced per work order once the call is closed, with labor, trip, diagnostic, parts and
refrigerant on separate lines so the owner can see what each part of the call cost.

## Applying a payment

Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice first unless the owner directs the payment to a named
invoice.

## A missing purchase order number

Where a purchase order number is required under the tier, an invoice issued without it is reissued
rather than treated as overdue.

### Illustration of the application order (hypothetical)

An account under the Demand Service Rate Programs carries three unpaid invoices raised in successive
months. A payment arriving with no direction from the owner is applied to the oldest of the three. Where
the owner directs that payment to the most recent invoice by naming it, it is applied to that invoice
instead, and the older two stand unpaid.

### Basis question

*The owner says an invoice cannot be paid because it carries no purchase order number, and the program
requires one.* That invoice is reissued rather than treated as overdue.

superseded_clauses: The invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date, counted in calendar days with the invoice day excluded and the due day included, and the account's own credit terms apply only where the program has no term of its own.
An invoice unpaid past its due day carries the tier's late fee on the unpaid amount for each month or part month it stays unpaid.
